title: Yearbook and Locker
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has spent three years perfecting the art of being fine — until a college essay prompt asks students to name a truth they've never told anyone, and the anonymous submissions start leaking to the whole school. When one of the leaked truths implicates Hazel's best friend Theo in something that could destroy them both, Hazel must decide whether loyalty means silence or confession. Racing through a championship season that suddenly matters in ways no one intended, Hazel discovers the leaks are orchestrated by someone hunting a darker secret buried in the academy's scholarship program itself. In the end, Hazel wins nothing on the field but everything that counts: he tells his own truth publicly, saves Theo from taking the fall alone, and forces the school to confront what it did to the scholarship kids who came before him — at the cost of the future he was supposed to be buying with his silence.
about_author: X. M. Voss is the pen name of a former boarding-school scholarship kid who spent years writing other people's stories before writing this one. They live near the coast, keep every yearbook they've ever been given, and still remember their locker combination.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Opening day of senior year at Ashgrove Academy: Hazel performs effortless belonging — right clothes, right laugh, locker decorated just enough. Privately, he catalogs the cracks: the tuition letter hidden in his sock drawer, the essay deadline looming. Emotional beat: the exhausting choreography of being 'fine' established.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the college essay prompt: 'Name a truth you have never told anyone.' The class goes silent in a way that feels electric. Hazel writes something safe and lies about it even to himself. Beat: the question lands like a splinter nobody can ignore.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A folded page appears in Hazel's locker — someone else's honest answer to the prompt, raw and devastating, signed only with an initial. He didn't put it there. Neither, it turns out, did anyone admit to. Beat: unease; the school's walls have started talking.

chapters.title: Theo's Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rowing captain Theo is carrying his own secret answer to the prompt — one involving money that appeared in his family's account the year he got into Ashgrove. He burns his draft. Beat: dread disguised as confidence; we see the secret before Hazel does.

chapters.title: The First Leak
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An anonymous account posts a student's truth online — a girl's confession about her eating disorder, stripped of context and mercy. The school erupts in performative sympathy and quiet cruelty. Beat: horror; honesty has become a weapon.

chapters.title: Scholarship Kids Stick Together
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and fellow scholarship student Priya compare notes: all the leaked truths so far came from financial-aid students. Someone is targeting them specifically. Beat: solidarity forming into fear; belonging was always conditional.

chapters.title: What Hazel Wrote
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, flashback-heavy. We finally learn Hazel's own essay truth: that he reported his father's crime to police at fifteen, and his family hasn't spoken since. He's never told anyone at Ashgrove. Beat: vulnerability; the reader now holds what the leaker wants.

chapters.title: Regatta
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Theo POV. The autumn championship regatta; Theo rows brilliantly while Hazel watches from the bank, both of them pretending the leak situation isn't tightening around the scholarship kids. Beat: borrowed joy; the last good weekend.

chapters.title: The Account Finds Theo
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The anonymous account posts a teaser: next leak involves 'a captain who bought his seat.' Hazel realizes it's Theo. Confronting him, Hazel gets half-truths and panic. Beat: betrayal's first sting; loyalty begins pulling against truth.

chapters.title: Priya's Theory
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya digs into Ashgrove's archives and finds a pattern: a decade ago, several scholarship students were quietly expelled after a scandal no one will name. She believes the leaker is one of them, or someone connected. Beat: mystery deepens; the present is haunted by the past.

chapters.title: The Deal Hazel Is Offered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An anonymous message reaches Hazel directly: expose Theo's secret himself, and his own truth stays buried — plus a donor will 'take care of' his college costs. Beat: temptation; survival has a price tag and it's his friend.

chapters.title: Midterm Week
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel avoids Theo, aces his exams, and hates himself efficiently. Ms. Okafor returns his essay draft with one note: 'This is true. Why does it read like an apology?' Beat: guilt sharpened into self-knowledge.

chapters.title: What Theo Did
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Full reveal: Theo's mother accepted hush money from a booster tied to the old scandal in exchange for Theo's silence about what he witnessed as a freshman. Theo didn't take the money — she did, to keep them housed. Beat: compassion complicates judgment; the secret is sadder than scandalous.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't Supposed to Happen
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The account posts Priya's truth instead of Theo's — her undocumented status — proving the leaker will burn anyone, deal or no deal. Hazel understands he was never being offered protection, just a slower order of execution. Beat: terror; the rules were always fake.

chapters.title: Alumni Weekend
chapters.summary: Hazel and Priya POV, alternating. At alumni events, they track down Marcus Webb, expelled ten years ago. He tells them the truth: the school covered up abuse by a beloved coach, and the scholarship kids who spoke up were destroyed for it. Beat: righteous anger; the pattern has a blueprint.

chapters.title: Who Holds the Locker Key
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Clues converge: the leaker has master key access and knows the old case intimately. Suspicion falls on Ms. Okafor — then pivots when Hazel finds the account's drafts folder mirrored on a school server used by Headmaster Lyle's office. Beat: vertigo; the villain may be the institution itself.

chapters.title: Championship Eve
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the eve of the national qualifier, the account announces its finale: tomorrow, during the championship, Theo's full story goes public. Theo asks Hazel to help him disappear before the race. Beat: heartbreak; loyalty demands Hazel choose between Theo's escape and the truth.

chapters.title: The Race That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Championship day. Hazel convinces Theo to row anyway — not to win, but to be visible, unashamed, surrounded by people when the leak drops. Ashgrove loses by inches. Beat: defiant grace; losing together beats winning alone.

chapters.title: The Leak That Matters
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Mid-crowd, phones light up: the account publishes not Theo's secret but the coach scandal files — ten years of them — plus proof Lyle orchestrated the original cover-up and has been using the essay leaks to find and silence anyone who might repeat history. Beat: climax detonation; the trap was aimed upward all along.

chapters.title: Hazel's Answer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With reporters arriving and Lyle spinning, Hazel takes the microphone at the post-race assembly and reads his own essay aloud — his father, his exile, his years of performing 'fine' — then names what the school did to Marcus Webb and the others. Beat: catharsis; the price of survival, refused.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Rotating POV: Hazel, Theo, Priya. Lyle resigns under investigation; Okafor is revealed as the leaker's ally, having fed the archive to force reckoning. Theo's mother faces consequences; Theo stays. Priya organizes scholarship students into something with power. Beat: bruised relief; truth cost everything except each other.

chapters.title: Yearbook and Locker
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. Spring: Hazel cleans out locker 214, signs yearbooks honestly for once, and mails his final college essay — the true one — to a school that isn't Ashgrove. He keeps the anonymous note that started it all. Beat: quiet hope; belonging, he finally believes, shouldn't require disappearing.
